doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27

title: Blanche's memories of the Brunies boys' pranks and Johnny Lala
summary: Blanche recalls the boys sleeping at her house, Johnny Lala staying over, and Abbie and Georgie's mischief, Chink Martin's tuba smeared with cheese, and pills in a player's dinner.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: We had a nice place. I lived in a beautiful place. Yeah, I love George. He was so nice. Nice step going up there. And I had some cops up in there. All them kids used to come up there and flop
up there. Johnny Lala too. He used to play cornet too.
Johnny Lala was a good friend of mine. I used to play with him in Brownlee's band. Yeah,

he's nice. He's a wonderful fellow. He's a good boy. He used to sleep at our house when he had to go on jobs like that. And they was afraid they wouldn't get up because he worked late at the market. He would take

sleep than they had upstairs you know. And they had cots up there. They were sleeping. Yeah. Gentlemen that fellow used to raise more Santa power at night and keep pillaging for them. Fetish scattered off.

Oh they was terrible. Especially that Abby and Georgie. Yeah. You wouldn't imagine the mischief that Abby can brew. That Abby is a case. I'm telling you he's a case. I don't know if you remember I'll see Lunes Yellow Lunes it was a couple

They all had supper before they go to play music one night at my house on Polk Street. Abby was there in Georgie. And right on the windowsill by the table I had a little vine like that of tablets for the bowels. Oh little little bit of things. What did Abby do but yellow? He mixed it in yellow's food.

man had such cranks. He was so sick of the Elmire pleasure ground. He doubled up. And Georgie was laughing. And laughing. And Abby put the corned down. He was rolling on the bandstand. I said what is all this about? Abby said you wouldn't know. He said you wouldn't know mama. He said you know them pills you had for Alfred on the windowsill. I put them in yellow's dinner. I said Abby ain't you ashamed. Ain't you ashamed of yourself. I said she had them all day long in the house. That's a shame. Oh he was sick. He was sick. All right. He was sick. I got it. But you see I had them for my boy. And I used to give him two. But God knows how many they put in a man's grub. I don't know. How many they put in his food. They take everything. They take limburger cheese all the skin and all that mess. And they shoved it in chink's tube and smeared it all around. Every time it was playing. He stunk out the golden room over there. Oh chink you stink. And all that poor fella he didn't know when he come home he told me he showed it to me. He wiped it out. He come home and showed it to me said they did that.
